summary.claim_boundary: This is evidence for multiplicity and target-conditioned distributed causal organization in the executed 13-run nanoGPT family. It does not assert geometric convergence, a unique owner, a unique minimal support set, complete higher-order identification, or universal abstraction in all systems.
identified_limits: Single-component sufficiency is not identifiable without a triple gate that leaves one component active.
The all-components-removed null is not identifiable without the four-component gate.
A complete support lattice, unique minimal sufficient set, and interactions above pair order are not identifiable.
A pair pattern compatible with backup or substitution cannot by itself exclude an unobserved higher-order interaction.
Necessity and sufficiency are contextual to the executed target, query, receiving state, component versions, and gate site.
summary.scientific_interpretation: The existing native interventions directly expose target-conditioned causal support organization: different concrete held-out instances retain the learned mod-23 relation under multiple different observed surviving configurations; single and pair gates produce target-boundary-specific necessity, pair-failure, and non-additive consequences; and these relations reorganize across formation, decline, and recovery.
